correctness.rationale: The k=1 overlap forces all binary codewords to have a common first symbol and opposite common last symbol. Complementation normalizes to 0...1. Every code is exactly a clique of fully enumerated unbordered words, with substring and pair-overlap constraints explicitly checked. Correct greedy-color independent classes bound clique size and sorted cheapest available lengths bound all completions; the ordered recursion exhausts all cliques. A Python stdlib checker reproducibly returns all nine (maximum-cardinality, minimum-total-length) pairs and verifies witnesses. Independent 0–1 MILP for n=10 returns 227 with zero gap. This is a complete finite proof and not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: A 2024 publication directly asks to minimize average length at prescribed non-overlap code cardinality. The complete maximum-cardinality binary finite spectrum for n=2..10 is a natural self-contained cutoff: n=10 has 295 allowable vertices and 20,758 incompatible pairs, and the exact sharp optimum saves 13 bits versus 24 ten-bit codewords. This is a meaningful discrete compression/synchronization invariant beyond mere correctness or a small arbitrary subcase.
